checks.name: Screw engagement vs insert / thread

value.label: measured

build_strategy.title: ODM customisation
build_strategy.explanation: Not designed from scratch. Products like this need a modem / optics / autonomy stack and years of certification work, so the realistic path is an ODM (original design manufacturer) with a close reference platform: you customise the enclosure, colours, display, sensors and software, and the ODM builds it on its certified base.
customisable: Behaviours / skills on the ODM's autonomy stack
not_customisable: Mobile base with drive, BMS and safety sensors

entry_cost.label: estimate
entry_cost.source_or_assumption: Typical first production run for this category (Platform licence + NRE ≈ $150k, shell moulds ≈ $60k, safety + certifications ≈ $40k) — industry range, not a quote

lead_time.label: estimate
lead_time.source_or_assumption: Frozen design → first production units (tooling, samples, certification), typical

path: Find an ODM with a close reference platform (size, chipset / modem bands or sensor, price tier) — shortlist 3 and get their reference designs
Customise what differentiates the product: enclosure and CMF (colours, materials, finish), display, sensors, buttons, packaging
Customise the software on the ODM's SDK / BSP (launcher, app policy, UI) and contract the update schedule

Certifications: carried over where the RF / electrical design is unchanged (modular approvals), redone where you change it (new antenna area, metal back, new radio) — plus the product-level declaration in each market
Engineering samples → pilot run (EVT/DVT/PVT) → mass production on the ODM line
build_strategy.certifications_note: Base-platform safety and radio reports reused; product-level safety (IEC 60335-1 / 62368-1), functional safety review of the arm.
assumptions: Estimates for a first production run; real MOQs and NRE come from quotes
ODM figures assume an existing reference platform close to the brief

checks.name: Interference between moving parts

value.label: measured
value.source_or_assumption: Boolean common of every part pair (OCCT), classified by the assembly joints; total 0.0 mm³

checks.threshold: 0 intersecting pairs > 0.01 mm³ between parts that move relative to each other (different rigid bodies, over their motion study) or across a parting line — CAD interference-check practice
checks.formula: V(A ∩ B) per pair of solids at the assembled pose and over each moving joint's motion study

checks.name: Overlaps inside rigid bodies (concept geometry)

value.label: measured
value.source_or_assumption: 7 pairs of rigidly joined parts interpenetrate (5 over 5 % of the smaller part)

checks.threshold: Parts of one rigid body should not interpenetrate: overlap > 5 % of the smaller part = concept geometry to pocket at detail design (warn); smaller overlaps are seats (info)
checks.formula: V(A ∩ B) for parts of the same rigid body that are not directly joined
notes: Bottom shell 3 ↔ Bin lip: 39565 mm³
Arm 4 ↔ Arm 6: 3010 mm³
M4 heat-set inserts ×4 ↔ Screw bosses: 133 mm³
Rear access panel ↔ M3 × 10 countersunk screws ×4: 111 mm³
M5 washers ×2 ↔ M5 × 14 socket screws ×2: 81 mm³

checks.name: Minimum clearance of moving parts

value.label: measured
value.source_or_assumption: Lower bound: no moving part has a neighbour within 12 mm (or no moving joint)

checks.threshold: Rolling / rotating part ≥ 1 mm running clearance to its surroundings (debris, moulding tolerance)
checks.formula: min over poses of d(moving subtree, other parts); revolute props 12 poses / 360°, buttons pressed 0.5 mm

checks.name: Screw engagement vs insert / thread

value.label: measured
value.source_or_assumption: Material under each screw measured by a line ∩ solid on both parts; flange capped at 2·d (counterbore), screw = shortest ISO length reaching the insert / thread

checks.threshold: Heat-set insert: boss holds the insert + 0.5 mm and the screw engages ≥ 80 % of it (McMaster-Carr 94459A insert data); tapped metal ≥ 1.5·d; thread-forming screw in plastic ≥ 2·d (EJOT DELTA PT design guide)
checks.formula: engagement = min(insert length, screw length − flange); boss depth = material of the threaded part
notes: Top shell 1 → Bottom shell 3: 4 × M3×12 + insert M3×5.7, engagement ≥ 5.7 mm, pass
Top shell 2 → Bottom shell 3: 2 × M2.5×10 + insert M2.5×4, engagement ≥ 4.0 mm, pass (1 position(s) without material on both parts)
Metal parts → Bottom shell 1: 4 × M3×12 (tapped), engagement ≥ 0.0 mm, warn (4 position(s) without material on both parts)
Bottom shell 2 → Bottom shell 1: 2 × M2.5×10 + insert M2.5×4, engagement ≥ 4.0 mm, pass
Ball bearings 6001-2Z (12×28×8) ×2 → Bottom shell 1: 4 × M3×12 (tapped), engagement ≥ 0.0 mm, warn (4 position(s) without material on both parts)
Body → Top shell 2: 4 × M3×12 + insert M3×5.7, engagement ≥ 5.7 mm, pass (2 position(s) without material on both parts)
Metal part → Body: 2 × M2.5×10 (tapped), engagement ≥ 5.0 mm, pass (1 position(s) without material on both parts)
Arm 5 → Arm 6: 2 × M2×8 (tapped), engagement ≥ 4.0 mm, pass
Dark part → Metal part: 2 × M2.5×10 (tapped), engagement ≥ 5.0 mm, pass
Arm 4 → Arm 5: 4 × M3×12 + insert M3×5.7, engagement ≥ 5.7 mm, pass
Arm 3 → Arm 4: 2 × M2.5×10 + insert M2.5×4, engagement ≥ 4.0 mm, pass
Arm 2 → Arm 3: 4 × M3×12 + insert M3×5.7, engagement ≥ 5.7 mm, pass

checks.name: Joint closure (build123d Joints)

value.label: measured
value.source_or_assumption: Each child re-placed from its joint frame with build123d RigidJoint / RevoluteJoint / LinearJoint.connect_to; 35 joints

checks.threshold: build123d joints re-place every part at its modelled pose: residual < 0.01 mm
checks.formula: |bbox centre after connect_to − modelled bbox centre|

checks.threshold: Every part touches the part it is joined to (contact ≤ 0.05 mm)
checks.formula: d(child, parent) ≤ 0.05 mm for every joint
